constraint1:
Constraint 1: Assign each operation of every job to exactly one of its eligible machines.
Constraint 2: Operations within each job must follow their prescribed processing order.
Constraint 3: A machine may process only one operation at a time; operations on the same machine must not overlap.
Constraint 4: The makespan must be at least the completion time of every job.
Constraint 5: All operation start times must be nonnegative.
Constraint 6: To respect the material loading order, the first operation of Job 1 must start no later than the first operation of Job 2. They may start at the same time.
Constraint 7: For every job, if two consecutive operations are assigned to different machines, at least 45 time units must elapse after the earlier operation finishes before the next operation starts, to allow transportation.
formula1: \begin{equation}B_{i,j+1} \geq B_{i,j} + \sum_{k \in K_{i,j}} pt_{i,j,k}X_{i,j,k} + 45 \times \left(1 - \sum_{k \in K_{i,j} \cap K_{i,j+1}} X_{i,j,k}X_{i,j+1,k}\right), \quad \forall i \in I, j \in \{1, ..., n_i-1\}\end{equation}#(Constraint 6)
code1:
# Constraint 6: To respect the material loading order, the first operation of Job 1 must start no later than the first operation of Job 2. They may start at the same time.
    model.addConstr(B[0, 0] <= B[1, 0], name="job1_start_before_job2_due_to_loading")

constraint2:
Constraint 1: Every operation must be allocated to one and only one compatible machine.
Constraint 2: For each job, an operation may start only after its preceding operation has finished.
Constraint 3: Operations assigned to a common machine must be scheduled without overlapping processing intervals.
Constraint 4: The overall completion time cannot be smaller than any individual job's completion time.
Constraint 5: No operation is allowed to start before time zero.
Constraint 6: To respect production priorities, the start time of the first operation of Job 3 must be no greater than that of Job 4. Simultaneous starts are allowed.
Constraint 7: For any job in the workshop, consecutive operations assigned to different machines require a transportation interval of at least 75 time units between the completion of the earlier operation and the start of the later one.
formula2: \begin{equation}B_{i,j+1} \geq B_{i,j} + \sum_{k \in K_{i,j}} pt_{i,j,k}X_{i,j,k} + 75 \times \left(1 - \sum_{k \in K_{i,j} \cap K_{i,j+1}} X_{i,j,k}X_{i,j+1,k}\right), \quad \forall i \in I, j \in \{1, ..., n_i-1\}\end{equation}#(Constraint 7)
code2:
# Constraint 7: To respect production priorities, the start time of the first operation of Job 3 must be no greater than that of Job 4. Simultaneous starts are allowed.
    model.addConstr(B[2, 0] <= B[3, 0], name="job3_start_before_job4_due_to_priority")

constraint3:
Constraint 1: Select exactly one machine from the eligible set for each operation of each job.
Constraint 2: Respect the specified precedence sequence among the operations of a job.
Constraint 3: On any given machine, processing intervals of different operations must be mutually exclusive.
Constraint 4: The makespan must cover the completion of all jobs.
Constraint 5: The start time of every operation must be greater than or equal to zero.
Constraint 6: To satisfy the process-flow requirement, Job 1 may begin its first operation only after or at the completion of the last operation of Job 2.
Constraint 7: For all jobs, whenever the next operation uses a different machine from the preceding operation, its start time must be at least 25 time units after the preceding operation's completion to allow material transfer.
formula3: \begin{equation}B_{i,j+1} \geq B_{i,j} + \sum_{k \in K_{i,j}} pt_{i,j,k}X_{i,j,k} + 25 \times \left(1 - \sum_{k \in K_{i,j} \cap K_{i,j+1}} X_{i,j,k}X_{i,j+1,k}\right), \quad \forall i \in I, j \in \{1, ..., n_i-1\}\end{equation}#(Constraint 8)
code3:
# Constraint 8: To satisfy the process-flow requirement, Job 1 may begin its first operation only after or at the completion of the last operation of Job 2.
    model.addConstr(B[0, 0] >= B[1, OpNum[1]-1] + quicksum(pt_table[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] * X[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[1][OpNum[1]-1][k] > 0), name="job1_start_after_job2_completion_due_to_flow")

constraint4:
Constraint 1: Each job operation is to be processed on exactly one machine capable of performing it.
Constraint 2: A job's operations must be processed in the required order, with each predecessor completed before its successor starts.
Constraint 3: Each machine has unit capacity and cannot process two operations simultaneously.
Constraint 4: The makespan cannot precede the finishing time of any job.
Constraint 5: Operation start times are restricted to zero or later.
Constraint 6: For process coordination, Job 1 must not start before Job 2 has finished its final operation. Job 1 may start exactly when Job 2 finishes.
Constraint 7: For any job, a change of machine between consecutive operations requires at least 65 time units for transportation after the earlier operation finishes and before the next one starts.
formula4: \begin{equation}B_{i,j+1} \geq B_{i,j} + \sum_{k \in K_{i,j}} pt_{i,j,k}X_{i,j,k} + 65 \times \left(1 - \sum_{k \in K_{i,j} \cap K_{i,j+1}} X_{i,j,k}X_{i,j+1,k}\right), \quad \forall i \in I, j \in \{1, ..., n_i-1\}\end{equation}#(Constraint 27)
code4:
# Constraint 6: For process coordination, Job 1 must not start before Job 2 has finished its final operation. Job 1 may start exactly when Job 2 finishes.
    model.addConstr(B[0, 0] >= B[1, OpNum[1]-1] + quicksum(pt_table[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] * X[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[1][OpNum[1]-1][k] > 0), name="job1_start_after_job2_completion_seq")

constraint5:
Constraint 1: For every operation, choose one eligible machine and assign the operation to that machine alone.
Constraint 2: All operations belonging to the same job must satisfy the given precedence relationships.
Constraint 3: Any two operations processed by the same machine must have non-overlapping processing intervals.
Constraint 4: Every job must finish no later than the makespan.
Constraint 5: Starting an operation at a negative time is prohibited.
Constraint 6: Under the parallel-processing requirement, Job 1 must start its first operation at or before the completion of the final operation of Job 2.
Constraint 7: If consecutive operations of any job are processed on different machines, allow at least 50 time units for transportation from the completion of the earlier operation to the start of the later operation.
formula5: \begin{equation}B_{i,j+1} \geq B_{i,j} + \sum_{k \in K_{i,j}} pt_{i,j,k}X_{i,j,k} + 50 \times \left(1 - \sum_{k \in K_{i,j} \cap K_{i,j+1}} X_{i,j,k}X_{i,j+1,k}\right), \quad \forall i \in I, j \in \{1, ..., n_i-1\}\end{equation}#(Constraint 28)
code5:
# Constraint 7: Under the parallel-processing requirement, Job 1 must start its first operation at or before the completion of the final operation of Job 2.
    model.addConstr(B[0, 0] <= B[1, OpNum[1]-1] + quicksum(pt_table[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] * X[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[1][OpNum[1]-1][k] > 0), name="job1_start_before_job2_completion_parallel")

constraint6:
Constraint 1: Each operation must receive exactly one assignment among its compatible machines.
Constraint 2: Within a job, the next operation cannot begin until the previous operation is complete.
Constraint 3: Machine processing must be sequential: no two operations on a machine may run at the same time.
Constraint 4: The makespan is required to be no less than the finishing time of each job.
Constraint 5: The earliest permissible start time for any operation is zero.
Constraint 6: For capacity scheduling, the start of Job 1 must be no later than the completion of Job 2. Starting Job 1 exactly when Job 2 finishes is permitted.
Constraint 7: For Job 3, consecutive operations assigned to different machines must have a transportation interval of at least 60 time units. The next operation cannot start until this interval has elapsed after the preceding operation completes.
formula6: \begin{equation}B_{3,j+1} \geq B_{3,j} + \sum_{k \in K_{3,j}} pt_{3,j,k}X_{3,j,k} + 60 \times \left(1 - \sum_{k \in K_{3,j} \cap K_{3,j+1}} X_{3,j,k}X_{3,j+1,k}\right), \quad \forall j \in \{1, ..., n_3-1\}\end{equation}#(Constraint 29)
code6:
# Constraint 8: For capacity scheduling, the start of Job 1 must be no later than the completion of Job 2. Starting Job 1 exactly when Job 2 finishes is permitted.
    model.addConstr(B[0, 0] <= B[1, OpNum[1]-1] + quicksum(pt_table[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] * X[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[1][OpNum[1]-1][k] > 0), name="job1_start_before_job2_completion_capacity")

# Constraint 29: For Job 3, consecutive operations assigned to different machines must have a transportation interval of at least 60 time units. The next operation cannot start until this interval has elapsed after the preceding operation completes.
    i = 2  # Job 3 (Python index 2)
    for j in range(OpNum[i] - 1):
        same_machine = quicksum(X[i, j, k] * X[i, j+1, k] for k in range(MacNum) 
                          if M_table[i][j][k] > 0 and M_table[i][j+1][k] > 0)
        model.addConstr(
            B[i, j+1] >= B[i, j] + quicksum(pt_table[i, j, k] * X[i, j, k] 
                                          for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[i][j][k] > 0) 
                        + 60 * (1 - same_machine),
            name=f"job3_transport_delay({j})"
        )

constraint7:
Constraint 1: An operation must be assigned to a single machine selected from its eligible machine set.
Constraint 2: The prescribed order of operations must be maintained separately for every job.
Constraint 3: Operations sharing a machine must be ordered so that one finishes before or when the next begins.
Constraint 4: The makespan must upper-bound the completion times of all jobs.
Constraint 5: Every operation must have a start time of at least zero.
Constraint 6: To meet the downstream assembly requirement, Job 1 must finish no later than Job 2. The two jobs may finish simultaneously.
Constraint 7: When Job 6 moves between machines for consecutive operations, the later operation must start at least 25 time units after the earlier operation finishes, allowing time to transport the job.
formula7: \begin{equation}B_{6,j+1} \geq B_{6,j} + \sum_{k \in K_{6,j}} pt_{6,j,k}X_{6,j,k} + 25 \times \left(1 - \sum_{k \in K_{6,j} \cap K_{6,j+1}} X_{6,j,k}X_{6,j+1,k}\right), \quad \forall j \in \{1, ..., n_6-1\}\end{equation}#(Constraint 7)
code7:
# Constraint 6: To meet the downstream assembly requirement, Job 1 must finish no later than Job 2. The two jobs may finish simultaneously.
    model.addConstr(B[0, OpNum[0]-1] + quicksum(pt_table[0, OpNum[0]-1, k] * X[0, OpNum[0]-1, k] for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[0][OpNum[0]-1][k] > 0) <= B[1, OpNum[1]-1] + quicksum(pt_table[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] * X[1, OpNum[1]-1, k] for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[1][OpNum[1]-1][k] > 0), name="job1_completion_before_or_equal_job2")

# Constraint 7: When Job 6 moves between machines for consecutive operations, the later operation must start at least 25 time units after the earlier operation finishes, allowing time to transport the job.
    i = 5  # Job 6 (Python index 5)
    for j in range(OpNum[i] - 1):
        same_machine = quicksum(X[i, j, k] * X[i, j+1, k] for k in range(MacNum) 
                          if M_table[i][j][k] > 0 and M_table[i][j+1][k] > 0)
        model.addConstr(
            B[i, j+1] >= B[i, j] + quicksum(pt_table[i, j, k] * X[i, j, k] 
                                          for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[i][j][k] > 0) 
                        + 25 * (1 - same_machine),
            name=f"job6_transport_delay({j})"
        )

constraint8:

Constraint 3: A machine cannot be occupied by more than one processing operation at any instant.
Constraint 4: The schedule's makespan must be at least as large as each job's completion time.
Constraint 5: All processing start times are constrained to be nonnegative.
Constraint 6: For final assembly coordination, the completion time of Job 1 must not exceed that of Job 2; equal completion times are allowed.
Constraint 7: For Job 7, a change of machine between consecutive operations requires a wait of at least 35 time units for transportation before the later operation can start.

# Constraint 8: For Job 7, a change of machine between consecutive operations requires a wait of at least 35 time units for transportation before the later operation can start.
    i = 6  # Job 7 (Python index 6)
    for j in range(OpNum[i] - 1):
        same_machine = quicksum(X[i, j, k] * X[i, j+1, k] for k in range(MacNum)

        model.addConstr(
            B[i, j+1] >= B[i, j] + quicksum(pt_table[i, j, k] * X[i, j, k] 
                                          for k in range(MacNum) if M_table[i][j][k] > 0) 
                        + 35 * (1 - same_machine),
            name=f"job7_transport_delay({j})"

Constraint 6: For synchronized delivery, Job 1 and Job 2 must finish at exactly the same time, meaning that their final operations have identical completion times.
